title: Théorie arithmétique. Théorie de Galois des motifs (1965) : notes manuscites (s.d.), tapuscrit (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: this is part of Grothendieck's 1965 notes on the 'Galois theory of motives'. The neighbouring 'previous page' is an unrelated Bourbaki errata sheet, likely just filed with the notes. The next page begins 'Motifs essentiellement abéliens et théorie du corps de classes'. The script on this page is very compressed, so the reading below is partly conjectural.

(1) Top of the page: two commutative squares.
- First square: gerbes G_φ → G at the top, G_X → G_Y at the bottom, with vertical arrows. Plausibly these are the motivic Galois gerbe G of a Tannakian category of motives M over k, and sub-/quotient gerbes attached to the subcategories generated by X, Y, or to a morphism φ. The exact meaning of the indices cannot be settled from this page.
- Second diagram: V → G → G_m via ε, with U → G^0 below, V ⊃ U, and G' pointing into G.
- Most natural reading: G is the motivic Galois group(oid) and G^0 its identity component (geometric motives, over k̄). ε : G → G_m is the Tate/cyclotomic character given by the action on the Tate motive Z(1). Then V = Ker ε and U = Ker(ε|G^0) = V ∩ G^0.
- G/G^0 = Γ = Gal(k̄/k), the Galois group of the Artin-motive part M^(0).

(2) Middle: change of base.
- The image suggests 'Soit k' une extension algébrique de k, d'où un foncteur M → M', M^(0) → M'^(0)'. Extension of scalars on motives (and on Artin motives) induces G' → G and Γ' → Γ, i.e. G'/G'^0 → G/G^0.
- The homomorphism is written G' ↪ G (injective), presumably identifying G' with the inverse image of the open subgroup Gal(k̄/k') of Γ.
- The whole system of squares for k' maps to the one for k.

(3) Conclusion ('En particulier, on trouve'):
- G'_{X'} → G_X and G'_{Y'} → G_Y.
- U' ≅ U and G'^0 ≅ G^0: the identity component and its Tate-kernel are insensitive to algebraic extension of the base field.

In modern terms this is the exact sequence 1 → G_{k̄} → G_k → Gal(k̄/k) → 1, with G_{k'} = π^{-1}(Gal(k̄/k')), together with the restriction of the Tate character t : G → G_m. These are standard expectations in Saavedra, Deligne–Milne, and Serre ('Propriétés conjecturales des groupes de Galois motiviques', 1994).
errors: No mathematical error is visible; the statements are expected (conditional on the standard conjectures, so that M is Tannakian with an exact Galois sequence).

Injectivity of G'→G and G'^0 ≅ G^0 require that motives over k̄ be the colimit over finite extensions and that Artin motives be exactly the finite part. This is asserted without proof (gap, not an error).
The meaning of G_φ, G_X, G_Y is not explained on this page.

ideas.what: Motivic Galois group(oid)/gerbe G with identity component G^0 and G/G^0 = Gal(k̄/k) (Artin motives)
ideas.where_published: Saavedra Rivano, Catégories tannakiennes (LNM 265); Grothendieck mentions motivic Galois groups in Récoltes et Semailles

ideas.what: Tate character ε: G→G_m and its kernels V = Ker ε, U = Ker ε ∩ G^0
ideas.modern_name: Cyclotomic/Tate character of the motivic Galois group; G^1 = Ker t
ideas.where_published: Serre, Propriétés conjecturales des groupes de Galois motiviques (1994)

ideas.what: Base change to an algebraic extension k'/k: G_{k'} ↪ G_k open subgroup with the same identity component
ideas.modern_name: Invariance of the identity component under finite extension

deep.surprise_reason: This is an early (1965) appearance of the motivic Galois group with its identity component, Tate character and base-change behaviour. Historically it confirms Grothendieck's early formulation, but the content is standard and has been in the literature since Saavedra, Deligne–Milne and Serre.
transcription_corrections: 'Soit M' une autre catégorie ... sur k' likely reads 'Soit k' une extension algébrique de k, d'où un foncteur ...' (extension of scalars), with M' the category of motives over k'.
'Γ'' → Γ' is probably Γ' → Γ (Galois groups of k' and k), with G'/G'^0 → G/G^0 beneath.
The arrow labelled 'G'' above G in the second diagram is probably G' → G (i.e. G' ↪ G), not a label.
